decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

<p class="MsoNormal" style="margin-bottom: 0cm; line-height: normal;">A Landscape Management Plan,
including species numbers/locations, long term design objectives, management,
responsibilities and maintenance schedules for the site shall be submitted to,
and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to. The Landscape
Management Plan shall be carried out as approved.&nbsp;<font face="Arial, sans-serif"><span style="font-size: 12pt;"><o:p></o:p></span></font></p>

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents:&nbsp;D 0 001 Rev 4, D 1 099 Rev I2, D 1 100 Rev 3, D 1 101 Rev 3, D 1 200 Rev 2, D 1 201 Rev 2, D 1 202 Rev 2, D 1 203 Rev 2, D 1300 Rev 2, D 1301 Rev 2, F1 100 Rev 3, F1 203 Rev 1, F1 204 Rev 1, D 1 002 Rev 1 D 1 003 Rev 1, D 1 004 Rev 1, D 1 005 Rev 1, D 1 006 Rev 1, C-011 Rev C1, C-012 Rev T2, C-021 Rev T2,&nbsp; F1 101 Rev 3, F1 201 Rev 1, F1 202 Rev 1, Landscape Management Plan (Bowles and Wyer, June 2023), Arboricultural Planning Statement Kiln House (ADAS, July 2023), Design and Access Statement (TP Bennett, March 2023), Heritage Statement (John Lowe Heritage, March 2023), Planning Statement (DP9, March 2023), Energy Statement (Ingine, March 2023), Specification for Conservation Works (Barton Engineers, March 2024), Construction Management Plan &amp; Material Management Plan (CMP Construct, November 2024), Kiln Protection Plan (Morgan Rae, June 2023), Drainage Strategy (Civilistix, 14 November 2024 - Rev: C), Kiln House - Brickwork Details (TP Bennett, June 2023), Building Damage Ground Movement assessment, Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (ADAS, July 2023), Biodiversity Net Gain Report (Assystem, July 2023), Basement Impact Review (A2 Site Investigation, March 2023), Ground Movement Assessment (A2 Site Investigation, March 2023).
<p>The development hereby permitted shall not commence until the existing drying shed and detached bungalow have been demolished.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development (except for the demolition of the drying shed and bungalow), a Method Statement for the repair and ongoing maintenance works to the Kiln and all associated curtilage listed buildings on site, shall be prepared by an accredited conservation specialist. The Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the commencement of development. The Method Statement shall contain such details to enable the Kiln to be taken off the Heritage at Risk Register, including:</p><ul><li>Details of all repairs works and materials including samples of mortar mix, colour, texture and pointing technique.</li><li>Details of how the Kiln shall be protected during the construction works for the approved development (extension).</li><li>Details of construction supervision for the monitoring and restoration and repair works to ensure such works are carried out in accordance with the approved Method Statement.</li><li>Details of ongoing maintenance of the Kiln and curtilage listed buildings on site.</li></ul>

<p>Prior to the commencement of any construction, demolition or preparatory works, the applicant shall submit to the Council for approval in writing a Final Construction Environment Management Plan (CEMP) which will provide full details of measures and timings, including method statements, drawings and specifications required in support of these, that will need to be implemented in order to:</p><p>a) safeguard features of ecological importance, including areas of semi-natural habitat, protected and priority species known or likely to use the site and its features for foraging, shelter, reproduction, commuting or other purposes, and the features of value to these species;</p><p>b) avoid impacts on habitats in areas adjoining the development site, and at its boundaries in particular;</p><p>c) prevent the spread of invasive non-native species (INNS) included on Schedule 9 of the Wildlife and Countryside Act and/or the current list produced by the London Invasive Species Initiative (LISI);</p><p>d) ensure that contractors and those responsible for overseeing the development will implement necessary measures in full.</p><p>The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved Final CEMP, in order to safeguard features of ecological importance, including areas of semi-natural habitat, protected and priority species known or likely to use the site and features for foraging, shelter, reproduction, commuting or other purposes, on which they wholly or partly depend.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development, the applicant shall provide to the Council for approval in writing a plan for the control and eradication of invasive non-native plants, with particular regard to the major infestation of New Zealand pigmy weed Crassula helmsii from within and around the pond and the wetland area and to inform the CEMP, taking account of the importance of the habitat in these areas to a range of species, including Great Crested Newt;</p><p>The development shall be undertaken in accordance with the approved Invasive Non Native Species Plan.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of development, the applicant shall submit to the Council for approval in writing:</p><p>a. Details of habitat creation and enhancement on the site</p><p>b. Maintenance and enhancement of wildlife access and commuting/foraging routes, e.g. for hedgehog, bats</p><p>c. wildlife shelter provision, to include:</p><p>i. ensuring that both of the wells will be retained and made accessible for use by roosting and hibernating bats</p><p>ii. installation of the following, commercially-produced, long-life, wildlife shelters (or similarly durable functional equivalents)</p><ul><li>Three Schwegler 3FF boxes (with or without inspection hatches) in suitable locations within a group of neighbouring trees</li><li>Two Schwegler 1N deep nest boxes</li><li>One Schwegler 1WK tawny owl nesting box</li></ul><p>The development shall be completed in accordance with the approved details. The wildlife shelters shall be installed prior to the completion of the development and shall be retained thereafter.</p>

<p>Notwithstanding the details shown on the approved drawings, the development hereby permitted shall not commence (save for demolition works) to be used in the construction of the external surfaces noted below have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority to be agreed in writing:</p><p>a) facing materials for the extension including roof;</p><p>b) windows;</p><p>c) doors;</p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so agreed and shall be retained as such thereafter.</p>
<p>The extension hereby permitted shall be constructed using Flemish bond to match the host dwellinghouse, Kiln House.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of the repair and restoration works (as per the approved Method Statement) of The Kiln, detailed information of The Heritage Interpretation Board (installed adjacent to the Kiln) and Plaque (fixed to the gate) shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Detailed information shall include the following:</p><ul><li>Size including scaled plans, elevations and sections.</li><li>Construction details including materials.</li><li>Design, layout and content of all text and images.</li><li>Location for installation.</li></ul><p>The Heritage Interpretation Board shall be installed prior to the commencement of Public Access in accordance with the approved details and shall be maintained in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.</p>

No site works or development shall commence until details of the levels of the building(s), road(s) and footpath(s) in relation to the adjoining land and highway(s), and any other changes proposed in the levels of the site, have been submitted to, and approved by, the local planning authority.&nbsp;The development shall be carried out in accordance with the details so agreed.

Notwithstanding the approved details, the development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until there has been a scheme of hard and soft landscape works for the site submitted to, and approved by the Local Planning Authority. Soft landscape works shall include: planting plans (at a scale not less than 1:100), schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes, plant container sizes (all at time of planting) and proposed numbers / densities. Hard landscape works shall include; details of boundary treatments (materials, scale of boundary, location) and details of hard surfacing materials to be used in the landscaping of the site.

All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the occupation of the building(s), or the completion of the development, whichever is the sooner.  Any existing or new trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development, die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting season, with others of a similar size and species, unless the local authority agrees any variation in writing.

<p>The development hereby approved shall not progress beyond damp proof course level until details for external lighting are submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval. Exterior lighting will be designed, positioned and operated so as to avoid impacts on nocturnal wildlife with particular regard to bat roosts, foraging areas and commuting routes, taking account of best practice guidance.</p><p>The development shall be completed in accordance with the approved details.</p>

<p>All tree removals (T36 and T55) and facilitation pruning (T2, T3, T18) detailed in Appendix 6 of the report, will be carried out prior to commencement of construction activities and prior to installation of tree protection measures. All tree work operations and facilitation pruning shall be carried out in accordance with BS3998:2010 ‘Recommendations for Tree Work’. The tree works schedule in Appendix 6 shall be adhered to and under no circumstances should the appointed contractor deviate from this schedule, unless approved in writing by the local authority.</p>

<p>The Arboricultural Method Statement (Section 8, pg 18 – 22 of ADAS report) and Tree Protection Plan (Appendix 2: Sheet 1 - 4 Tree Protection Plans) submitted in support of the application shall be adhered to in full, subject to the pre-arranged tree protection monitoring and site supervision, detailed in Appendix 10 / Sequence of Events after Planning Approval. The completed schedule of site supervision and monitoring of protection measures should be submitted to the Local Planning Authority for approval within 28 days of completion of the development, to ensure compliance with tree protection details and to provide evidence of compliance through supervision and monitoring / spot checks, for which the appointed tree consultant will need to be retained.</p>

<p>The repair and restoration of the Kiln and all associated curtilage listed buildings on site shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Method Statement within 12 months of the implementation of the permission (the extension).&nbsp; A Statement prepared by the accredited conservation specialist shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority&nbsp;within
one month of the completion of the repair and restoration works&nbsp;to confirm that the repair and restoration works were completed in accordance with the approved Method Statement.</p>
description: Single storey side to rear glazed link extension with excavation to create basement level; external alterations (demolition of ancillary building and drying shed)
